To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have measured the dust emissivity index βmm of the interstellar medium in the Milky Way to be about 1.6 in the densest molecular regions and about 1.5 in the more diffuse atomic regions, and that this difference is related to the amount of molecular gas along each line of sight.

we detect a correlation of the dust emissivities in the far-infrared (FIR) and millimetre (mm) bands with the optical depth at 100 μm in the Galactic plane and that we find a spectral index of the FIR-mm dust emission of β ∼ 1:54 for low dust optical depth regions (τ353 ∼ 10−5), and β ∼ 2 for high optical depth regions (e.g. molecular clouds).

we detect a correlation of the dust emissiv- ity spectral index at millimetre frequencies with the dust optical depth, that this is likely due to a change in the dust grain properties, that this is consistent with an evolution of dust emissivity related with the fraction of molecular hydrogen along the line of the sight, that the correlation between the dust spectral index and optical depth is not due to the free-free emission, and that the two-level system and ferromagnetic particles models can explain the results

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the emissivity index β of the dust emission is a function of the dust properties, and in particular of the dust temperature, the dust optical depth, and the fraction of molecular to atomic gas.

the Planck data show a correlation of the dust emissive properties in the 100-353 GHz range with the dust optical depth, and this is consistent with a correlation of the emissive properties with the fraction of molecular hydrogen along the line of the sight.
we are observing the evolution of the dust properties in the ISM, from atomic to molecular, and the dust properties are changing with the density and composition of the medium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the emissivity index at millimetre wavelenghts is correlated with the dust optical depth, and that this correlation can be explained with a model of the dust emission that includes two-level systems and/or magnetic dipole emission.
the dust emissivity is not a universal quantity but depends on the local physical conditions.
the dust emission at millimetric wavelengths in the Galactic Plane can be explained by two components, one that is related to the atomic gas and the other that is related to molecular gas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
dust emission in the diffuse interstellar medium is well described by a modified blackbody with a spectral index of about 1.55.
the emissivity index βmm is correlated with the optical depth at 3 mm.
the dust emissivity in the millimetre band is higher than in the sub-millimetre band, and that this difference is correlated with the dust column density.
